channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: Six-vehicle M25 crash between the M11 and Waltham Abbey brings hour-long delays to morning rush
item.description: Two of the four anticlockwise lanes near Waltham Abbey had reopened after the pile-up, with Essex Police saying nobody was reported hurt.

item.title: Commissioner gives Essex residents until 25 November to have a say on police and fire funding for 2027/28
item.description: Roger Hirst, the Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner for Essex, has extended his precept survey by two weeks after more than 750 responses.

item.title: Agency nurse told Colchester care home colleague he would 'kill' his whole family, panel finds
item.description: A Nursing and Midwifery Council panel found Rupesh Patel, 40, was drunk on a night shift at The Oaks care home in Colchester when he threatened a colleague, and he is set to be struck off.

item.title: Developer appeals over lack of decision on 910 green belt homes at Billericay's Foots Farm
item.description: Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee was asked to say how it would have decided the Great Burstead scheme, after an appeal was lodged because no decision had been made. Officers backed the plan, which offers more than £20 million in contributions.

item.title: Basildon councillors confirm refusal of 175 green belt homes at Little Burstead
item.description: Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee agreed the formal grounds for turning down homes west of Tye Common Road, near Billericay, going against officers' advice to approve.

item.title: Tendring councillors to vote on sending Local Plan for 1,069 homes a year to a government inspector
item.description: Tendring District Council's local plan committee meets on 17 November to decide whether to recommend submitting the plan, with Kirby Cross, Brightlingsea, Bradfield and Frinton sites drawing most objections.

item.title: Maldon scraps area planning committees and councillor call-in as new national rules take effect
item.description: Maldon District Council now has one 13-member Planning Committee, with most applications decided by officers under a new national scheme of delegation.

item.title: Maldon's share of the halted Mid Essex unitary council set-up costs put at about £26,000
item.description: Maldon District Council councillors have asked for a full breakdown, including officer time, of spending on the Mid Essex council plan before the government paused the Essex shake-up.

item.title: Essex's two biggest reservoirs down to 37% full as hosepipe ban drags on
item.description: Hanningfield and Abberton, which supply much of mid and south Essex, are below average for the time of year, Essex & Suffolk Water says, and the company is asking customers to keep saving water.

item.title: Suspected drug-drivers in Essex barred from driving for up to six weeks while police investigate
item.description: Essex Police says it is one of the first forces in the country to use bail conditions this way, as drug-driving arrests across the county keep rising.

item.title: Senior doctors' walkout that threatened Harlow hospital appointments is paused for pay talks
item.description: Consultants at Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow and across England will no longer strike later this month after the British Medical Association paused action to negotiate with the government.

item.title: Essex's first frost of the autumn expected as Chelmsford is forecast to drop to minus 1C on Friday night
item.description: Clear, dry weather across Essex brings sharp overnight falls in temperature before milder, wetter air returns at the weekend, the Met Office forecast shows.

item.title: Roper twins back at the University of Essex after double Commonwealth Games bronze for Wales
item.description: The Ipswich-born gymnasts won their medals within an hour of each other in Glasgow and are now back studying at the Colchester campus.

item.title: Pedestrian suffers potentially serious leg injury at Harlow crossing as police seek white or silver car
item.description: Essex Police say the car is reported to have gone through red lights at the Old House Croft crossing near Burnt Mill School in Harlow on Halloween evening and then left the scene.

item.title: Colchester curry house takes national Restaurant of the Year title
item.description: A Colchester Indian restaurant has been named Restaurant of the Year at the National Curry Awards.

item.title: Colchester United's home game with Fleetwood Town switched to Sunday 20 December
item.description: The League Two match moves back 24 hours so Fleetwood can recover from their Carabao Cup quarter-final against Everton.

item.title: Half-term getaway gives Stansted its busiest day ever with 109,881 passengers
item.description: October brought 2.79 million travellers through the Uttlesford airport, up 4.2% on the same month last year.

item.title: Brentwood centre for rape and sexual assault survivors reopens after refit with new aftercare rooms
item.description: The Essex Sexual Assault Referral Centre, paid for by the county's police commissioner with Essex Police, stays in the county so survivors need not travel elsewhere.

item.title: Thurrock academy trust puts school events for parents on hold, leaving nativity plays in doubt
item.description: Catalyst Academies Trust, which runs five schools in Thurrock including Benyon in South Ockendon, has written to parents after a row over a young sibling's attendance at events.

item.title: Southend council says it cannot step in to reopen Leigh North Street school's shut swimming pool
item.description: A report for Monday's cabinet says the pool's future is a matter for the school, despite a petition signed by more than 2,500 people.

item.title: GMB opens strike ballot at G4S Cash in Harlow, raising prospect of action before Christmas
item.description: Staff at the cash handling site are under a pay freeze, the union says, and voting runs until midday on 25 November.

item.title: Battery packs set a bin lorry alight in Colchester's Tangerine Close
item.description: Firefighters were called just after midday on Wednesday when batteries thrown out with the rubbish caught fire inside a refuse vehicle.

item.title: Southend United's Kieron Dyer banned for one match and goalkeeping coach Anssi Jaakkola for six
item.description: Both were sent off against Halifax Town and have also been fined, so Dyer misses Saturday's home game with Aldershot Town.

item.title: Thurrock cabinet asked to scrap modular council homes plan and write off almost £400,000
item.description: Officers say the Thurrock scheme, which included homes for Afghan families who supported British forces, no longer offers value for money.

item.title: Festoon lights back on Southend Pier for the first time in over 20 years, with switch-on set for Saturday
item.description: More than a mile of lights will run the length of the pier, launching an evening of festive events across the city on 14 November.

item.title: Developer seeks permission for 170 homes on Hutton green belt land
item.description: A planning application has been lodged for new housing on green belt land at Hutton, near Brentwood, close to a country park.

item.title: Essex Freemasons hand air ambulance charity another £11,000 and pledge more for 2027
item.description: Essex & Herts Air Ambulance has received a further donation from Essex Freemasons, part of a five-year commitment worth £50,000.

item.title: Two 18-year-olds and a boy of 17 arrested after man is stabbed in Basildon's East Walk
item.description: The man went into a nearby business for help on Tuesday evening and was taken to hospital; his injuries are not thought to be life-threatening.

item.title: Some Tendring households miss bin collections as council cites technical problems
item.description: The Gazette reports that bins went unemptied in parts of the Tendring district because of what were described as technical issues.

item.title: State Fayre claims a UK camping festival first with an all-female headline bill at Hylands Park
item.description: The Chicks, Kacey Musgraves and Shania Twain will top the country and Americana festival in Chelmsford from 18 to 20 June 2027.

item.title: Figures reveal 1,600 litter reports about Essex parks
item.description: Reports of litter logged about parks across Essex have been counted over a five-year period, new figures show.

item.title: Clacton Town given temporary licence to keep playing at council-owned Rush Green Bowl
item.description: Tendring council says the short-term deal covers the rest of the 2026/27 season while it prepares an open tender for a longer lease on the ground.

item.title: NHS Essex asks new parents how useful its safer sleep advice for babies really was
item.description: An anonymous five-minute survey on Essex Virtual Views is open to recent and expectant parents until 5pm on Monday 23 November.

item.title: Essex Freemasons hand air ambulance charity another £11,000 and pledge more for 2027
item.description: The gift to Essex & Herts Air Ambulance takes the Province's five-year support to £50,000 once next year's pledge is paid.

item.title: Eastwood dog owner to be sentenced in December after 15 German shepherds were rescued from his home
item.description: Terence Snooks was convicted of 15 animal welfare offences after a joint council and police raid, in what officers called one of the worst neglect cases they had seen in 30 years.

item.title: Harlow Rugby Club to host free prostate cancer blood tests for 96 men in December
item.description: The club is teaming up with men's health charity CHAPS and the Matchroom Charitable Foundation for a screening day at Latton Park.

item.title: Refurbished cafe opens at Chafford Gorges Nature Discovery Centre in Chafford Hundred
item.description: The Essex Wildlife Trust cafe at the Chafford Hundred nature centre serves coffee, tea and cake on Fridays to Sundays and is taking bookings for parties and clubs.

item.title: Cafe at Chafford Gorges Nature Discovery Centre reopens after refurbishment
item.description: Essex Wildlife Trust's cafe in Chafford Hundred serves coffee, tea and cakes from 10am to 4pm, Friday to Sunday.

item.title: Thurrock Council launches review of its libraries and asks residents for their views
item.description: A borough-wide needs assessment will shape a new Library Strategy, with the council pointing to housing growth, transport changes and local government reorganisation.

item.title: Colchester United edge Ipswich Town U21 on penalties after goalless EFL Trophy dead rubber
item.description: Thimothée Lo-Tutala saved twice in the shootout as the U's took the bonus point at the JobServe Community Stadium.

item.title: Basildon councillors to vote on backing a permanent war memorial, taking up D-Day veteran Don Sheppard's campaign
item.description: A motion from the Mayor of Basildon goes to full council on 17 November, asking officers to look at sites, designs and funding for a memorial for Basildon and Laindon.

item.title: Young carers group and Wickford Town youth club among first winners from Basildon's £100,000 community fund
item.description: Kool Carers gets £4,850, Wickford Town FC £2,950 for a new youth club and Friends of Wickford Memorial Park £1,800, with 17 more projects shortlisted.

item.title: Hollyoaks creator Sir Phil Redmond tours Basildon as town prepares its UK Town of Culture bid
item.description: Basildon is one of 15 towns shortlisted from 398 to become the first UK Town of Culture in 2028, with full bids due by 30 November.

item.title: Temporary housing for homeless families drives Basildon Council towards a £3.8m overspend this year
item.description: A half-year report warns reserves of £41.1m could be largely used up by 2029/30 if gaps keep being covered from savings, though it calls that a scenario rather than a forecast.

item.title: Bus journeys starting in Thurrock to cost no more than £2 from Monday under festive fare cap
item.description: The Department for Transport is paying for the scheme, which arrives ahead of a planned national cap at the same level from January.

item.title: Police ask for dash cam footage after man in his 80s dies following Mount Bures crash on Hall Road
item.description: A woman in her 70s is still being treated in hospital after a car struck both pedestrians on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Harlow sets 21 November for Christmas lights switch-on in revamped Market Square, with ice rink opening the same day
item.description: Harlow Council has published the timings for its Christmas launch, promising the town's biggest festive display yet.

item.title: More than 23 years of jail terms over Epping Bell Hotel disorder after Loughton man, 34, is locked up
item.description: Keith Silk was given two years and 11 months at Chelmsford Crown Court for violent disorder and criminal damage outside the hotel.

item.title: People sleeping rough in Essex offered free flu jabs for the first time, with clinics in Southend and Grays
item.description: NHS Essex is running dedicated clinics after national eligibility was widened to people aged 16 and over who are homeless.

item.title: National Highways asks Thurrock to hold off on 200-home Grey Goose Farm scheme in Grays until February as residents object
item.description: Persimmon wants outline permission for homes north of Long Lane, but the roads agency says more modelling is needed on the busy North Stifford junction first.

item.title: Thurrock's last chance to comment on plan for nearly 29,000 homes has now closed
item.description: The plan, which runs to 2044, will now go forward to an independent inspector, with West Horndon earmarked for about 10,000 of the new homes.

item.title: North Essex councils' joint Link scheme has backed 149 firms so far this year, 22 of them in Colchester
item.description: Most businesses helped had not used council-funded support in the previous year, Colchester City Council says, and a drop-in session for firms is planned in the city next month.

item.title: Underfloor heating firms behind Fastwarm pass £150,000 raised for Little Havens children's hospice
item.description: The business partners have backed the Thundersley hospice for 18 years and have now joined Havens Hospices' corporate membership scheme.

item.title: Parish councils object as Saturday deadline nears for comments on data centre at Little Canfield's old Crumps Farm landfill
item.description: Little Canfield and Great Canfield parish councils have raised fears over contaminated land, water supply and the countryside as Essex County Council weighs the 10,240 sq m scheme near Dunmow.

item.title: Maldon MP and council leader urge Home Secretary to drop plan for asylum seekers to live in Tillingham
item.description: The Home Office has approved buying a property in the Dengie village for up to six people under its national dispersal scheme, Maldon District Council says.

item.title: Wickford station's new ticket office opens as Greater Anglia rebuild nears the finish
item.description: Rayleigh and Wickford MP Mark Francois opened the ticket office on Monday, with the rest of the station upgrade due by the end of 2026.

item.title: Walk-in X-rays and new scans coming to St Margaret's diagnostic centre in Epping from mid-December
item.description: Blood tests move into the new community diagnostic centre at St Margaret's Hospital on 16 November, with X-ray, ultrasound and liver scans following on 14 December.

item.title: Microsoft picks Colchester City Council as the only UK council in its latest AI case study
item.description: The council says it measures how its staff use digital tools and targets training where confidence is low, rather than relying on technology alone.

item.title: Air ambulance charity draws more than 150 women to North Weald event on careers in emergency flight medicine
item.description: Essex & Herts Air Ambulance says women already make up about a third of its doctors and paramedics, well above the UK picture, and wants to go further.

item.title: Essex pair Jordan Cox and Sam Cook keep their places in England's Test squad for the South Africa tour
item.description: The two Essex players are among 15 picked by England for a three-Test series that starts in Johannesburg on 17 December.
